text.tspan: A calendar gives plans a place in time.
There is more than one way to make a realistic plan. In my experience, practical preparation and
attention to others are two useful starting points.
One reason is that reviewing a specific experience teaches more than a vague judgement. For instance,
we describe one habit that helped us instead of calling the whole year good or bad. This prevents a
small difficulty from taking over the experience. It also leaves us more time to notice what is happening.
Another reason is that a small next step is easier to act on than a broad promise. For example, we
choose a ten-minute practice session and put it on the calendar. This approach recognises that the
experience belongs to more than one person and that different people may need different things.
These examples show why preparation and consideration work well together. We do not have to control
every detail. We can make a sensible arrangement and remain ready to respond.
BUILD YOUR OWN · State a focused main idea. Develop one supporting reason in each body paragraph, with a concrete
example. Conclude by connecting the two reasons without introducing a new argument. Use the structure as a model; write
about an experience of your own.
Explain the meaning before looking at the model answer. What two reasons support the main idea? Explain one example.
